newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi paper calls for dismissal of U.N.'s Ekeus.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi paper calls for dismissal of U.N.'s Ekeus.

text.p: The newspaper of President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday on Tuesday called for the dismissal of Rolf Ekeus, chairman of the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) on Iraq.

"The world public opinion...should call for the sacking of Ekeus because his targets, known and clear, are for the obstruction of any possible chance to lift the embargo on Iraq," Babel said in a front-page editorial.
It accused Ekeus of lying and said his primary aim was to serve U.S. interests, not to fulfil his mandate under U.N. ceasefire resolutions that ended the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
"The new trip by Ekeus will be shrouded with new lies and expected fabrications," Babel said.
Ekeus is scheduled in Baghdad on Thursday for talks with Iraqi leaders to defuse a U.N.-Iraq standoff over long-range missiles.
Babel said Ekeus's insistence that Iraq was still hiding banned missiles was a game which he jointly "played with America to delay the implementation of the oil-for-food deal".
It was the second attack in Iraq's press on Ekeus in seven days. The official al-Iraq newspaper last week accused the envoy of "aggressive remarks" and attempts to escalate tensions with Iraq.

Sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait can be lifted only when Ekeus's commission decides that Iraq has scrapped all of its weapons of mass destruction including missiles with ranges greater than 150 km (93 miles).
